correctness.rationale: For n=∏p_i^{a_i}, four equal divisor-sum parts imply σ(n)/n≥4. For any prime-power factor, A_a(p)=∑_{j=0}^a p^{-j}<p/(p−1); if m prime-factor slots remain, every continuation is bounded above by R times the Euler factors of the m smallest unused primes. Candidate next-prime upper envelope R·p/(p−1)·E(p,m−1) decreases with p and tends to R; induction over smaller Ω establishes every proper prefix R<4 and hence rigorous termination for Ω≤8 without a guessed prime bound. Independently coded exact Fraction depth-first search returned no σ≥4n integers for Ω=1..7 and exactly 27720,32760,120120,180180,235620 for Ω=8, matching the source traversal counts (1,1,1,1,1,3,8,33 nodes; 58 Ω=8 prime trials, maximum tested 19). Independent distinct exponent-partition/permutation scan of all 22 partitions of Ω=8 finds exactly three viable patterns and all lower-layer maxima <4; this crosschecks pruning independently. Parsed actual partitions.json blob e00f0240... via GitHub and independently reconstructed each complete divisor set and bin sums: all five four-part partition certificates verify, with 96,96,128,144,144 divisors. Exact ratios 312/77,4,576/143,224/55,3744/935 and Ω=8 verified. Program execution alone is not a global proof: the rigorous envelope, induction and termination justify exhaustion.

OEIS A204831 lists only four of five examples, while OEIS A392936 lists the fifth as primitive four-abundant without a four-layered partition certificate.
Five explicit divisor partitions checked against complete divisor multisets and exact σ(n)/4 sums.
value.rationale: The smallest total number Ω of prime factors permitting a four-way equal divisor-sum partition is an intrinsic natural boundary, distinct from the smallest numerical example. The exact five-element equality fiber (including 235620 beyond the displayed 31-term four-layered list) is a motivated complete classification and proves a nontrivial equivalence between a necessary abundancy inequality and actual layeredness in this minimal layer. The witness partitions and mathematically terminating unbounded-prime search supply precise facts useful for future k-layered and divisor-sum multiplicity investigations. This does not claim classification at Ω≥9 or a general abundance-to-partition theorem.
